author: Sam Example
writings:
Most finance teams don't have an approvals problem. They have an inbox problem.

We spent a year watching controllers chase sign-offs over email. The fix wasn't a new form. It was one place to see who is waiting on whom.

What's the one approval that always stalls for you?

9 days.

That's how long month-end took at the first company we worked with. Now it's 4.

No magic. We moved approvals out of email and put a deadline on each one.

Short post today. Back to building.

I used to think more features would win deals.

They don't. Clarity does. Every customer we lost last year understood our product less than the one they chose.

So this quarter we are deleting things.

Hiring note: we are looking for an engineer who likes boring, reliable software.

If you get excited by an audit log that never misses a row, talk to me.

Three things I've learned selling to controllers:

1. They read everything.
2. They hate surprises.
3. They remember who was honest about limits.

Write for that reader.

Small win this week: a customer closed the quarter without a single approval reminder.

Nobody noticed. That's the point.
